unit.title: Numbers and Operations Around Us
unit.about_unit: Explores how human travel, trade, measurement, and recording large quantities led to five-digit numbers (ten thousands), multi-digit multiplication, division arrays, and multiplicative reasoning.

facilitation_guide.headline: Real-World Contexts
facilitation_guide.text: Connect numbers with train tickets, odometer readings, and village populations.

facilitation_guide.headline: Base-10 Manipulatives
facilitation_guide.text: Emphasize grouping 10 of any unit into 1 of the next higher unit using visual tokens.

chapter.title: Animal Jumps
chapter.tagline: Skip counting, common multiples, meeting spots on number lines, and mystery multiplier boxes
chapter.overview: A frog jumps 2 steps at a time, a rabbit jumps 3 steps, and a kangaroo leaps 5 steps. Where will they land together? Through dynamic animal jumps, students discover multiples, least common multiples (LCM), and crack function rules in mystery multiplier boxes.

sections.title: The Mystery Multiplier Box: Input-Output Machines
sections.subtitle: Discovering hidden functional multiplication rules

storyNarrative.dialogue: Look at this magical box! When 3 goes in, 18 comes out. When 5 goes in, 30 comes out! What is the box multiplying by?

concept.heading: Function Rule Identification
concept.keyRule: Output = Input × Multiplier (18 ÷ 3 = 6; 30 ÷ 5 = 6. The multiplier is 6).

sections.title: Common Multiples & The Meeting Spot
sections.subtitle: Finding the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of two or three numbers

storyNarrative.dialogue: Freddy jumps 2 steps, Ruby jumps 3 steps, and I jump 5 steps! The very first spot where all three of us land together is step 30!

concept.heading: Least Common Multiple (LCM)
concept.keyRule: The LCM is the smallest non-zero common multiple shared by two or more numbers. LCM(2, 3, 5) = 30.
